Incorporating the April 2022 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) into the assessment of the May 4, 2022 FOMC statement and the May 2022 Financial Stability Report (FSR):

- Credit supply to businesses still supportive: Banks reported easing standards on C&I loans to large and middle‑market firms and stronger loan demand tied to inventory, accounts receivable, equipment, and plant investment. Some price terms (spreads on credit lines) eased. This supports the statement’s note of strong business investment and tempers the FSR’s more negative tone.
- CRE credit broadly steady with a positive tilt: Standards largely unchanged for construction/land development and nonfarm nonresidential, with some easing for multifamily—another sign of still‑accommodative credit availability in early 2022.
- Household credit mixed: Banks reported weaker demand for residential real estate loans as rates rose, but eased standards for credit cards and stronger demand for HELOCs and auto loans—suggesting consumers still had access to credit even as mortgage activity cooled.
- Cross‑border caution: Foreign banks tightened C&I standards, a mild headwind, consistent with broader global risk concerns cited by the FSR.
- Net read: While inflation is elevated and policy tightening (rate hikes and QT) points to a more challenging backdrop, the SLOOS indicates domestic bank credit conditions remained accommodative in Q1 2022, partially offsetting FSR-identified vulnerabilities. Overall tone remains negative but less so than an FSR‑only read.
